stem.en: A state takes a fixed proportion of the produce, generally one-sixth, as tax on land. A village's harvest falls from 60 sacks to 30 sacks. What happens to the tax?

text.en: It stays at 10 sacks, because a tax is the same amount every year.
It falls from 10 sacks to 5 sacks, because the share stays at one-sixth.
It falls to nothing, because a state cannot tax a poor harvest.
It rises to 15 sacks, because the state must make up for the bad year.

explanation.en: The tax was a share of what the field produced. One-sixth of 60 is 10, and one-sixth of 30 is 5. The share stays the same, so the amount falls with the harvest. A fixed amount would stay at 10 sacks, which is option a. This is why a poor harvest also meant less revenue for the state.

hints.en: Work out one-sixth of 60, then one-sixth of 30.
